# R444 — upstream scope, functional adoption and comparison audit

Date: 2026-10-14 (Asia/Tokyo)
Mode: source/report read-only audit. No source or Git mutation, build, test, AST, GPU, process, environment, private-JSON, or raw-log inspection. The only write is this report.

## Scope and identity pins

User intent supplied for this audit: Niko1221/Strata is the only upstream; this is a personal-PC fork with no planned contribution upstream; CUDA/HIP are outside the work scope. XeStrata is a reference for benchmarking and useful architecture/implementation ideas, not a second upstream whose full feature set must be ported.

Compared committed trees: feature/sycl @ 4fa478f50f8da396e651e3ae862f8b1849d49b54; main @ beddab2fd6b61631d73b39b7484bc9a585ebe1de; K (feat/strata-upstream-sync-skill) @ 97f8b40ca99ec298c24d7ecc7b270e530d43194d; Z (feat/layer-major-bulk-upload) @ 28a7b9ae7ca5eba28eecd65f6453a7479c04fce8. The supplied retained pristine Niko snapshot is v0.1.43 @ 7695859aa13afb248bdb4d36f9b2e95707db079d. This is the latest pinned/reviewed release in the reports read here, not a claim about a newer upstream default-branch head.

## Findings

### Upstream and branch identity

- feature/sycl's CMake project version is Strata 0.1.38; main is 0.1.39. Neither is the reviewed Niko v0.1.43 baseline.
- Z and K are XeStrata-derived trees. Their CMake identifies XeStrata's integrated upstream as 0.1.40.2, commit e8ca9af, Xe revision 3. Z is Linux-only in CMake and applies Xe naming/build assumptions. Do not call either tree “Niko v0.1.43 integrated” as a whole.
- The official Niko v0.1.43 server source SHA256 is 55ee9d1160f0da457cabe6f9dfea9884296b6d70fd3d14abd4ed42e6f79dd72b. Z/K's adapted server SHA256 is e55ea984e0f64009f9fc32ed94439157c2aa523fea5fe0222fb60ffd9bb031dd. This is source evidence of a port/adaptation, not file identity or complete release parity.

### Actual non-inference feature presence

The Z/K actual server tree contains substantial v0.1.43-derived functionality: Responses API/context-overflow mapping, logit-bias handling, reasoning-effort controls, context/queue behavior, answer-budget reserve, reasoning-tail loop detection, held-tool-argument stream keepalive, frozen-engine watchdog, and conversation-cache Monitor view. The code markers and request paths are in current serve/server.py; serve/responses.py, serve/logit_bias.py, and serve/cache_drop.py are present. Z/K also have serve/replicas.py, serve/cpu_affinity.py, setup/server --replicas configuration, and related tests/CLI integration. The history identifies 0691bcdf as shared v0.1.43 functionality, c617512e as server integration, and de1bfe79 as the commit that introduced the four R300 server markers and replica/CPU-affinity path into the later source tree.

This is selective/adapted implementation in Z/K, not proof that every Niko 0.1.43 setup/server/tool behavior is present. The upstream-only Windows serve/winjob.py contract is absent; Z's CMake rejects non-Linux. Treat that as a support-boundary difference: irrelevant if this fork remains Linux-only, material if personal-PC Windows support is required. Upstream Windows prevent_sleep is similarly not a Linux requirement. The multi-GPU replica feature is present in source but is optional and does not need to be part of a one-GPU acceptance plan.

feature/sycl and main predate this import. Their CMake versions are 0.1.38/0.1.39, and they do not contain the later server-import commits. Their ancestry in Z does not change that. The relevant actual code is on Z/K's current trees.

### Reports whose findings are snapshot-specific or superseded

- R300 compared the earlier combined tree @ 9b03c18 to Niko v0.1.43 and correctly found four absent server behaviors at that snapshot. Those four are present in later Z/K source via de1bfe79; do not carry R300's gap list forward as current Z findings.
- R302 found replicas and Linux affinity absent from its earlier baseline @ 3141c18. Z/K now contain those paths. R302's one-engine-vs-replicas explanation remains valid, and replicas are outside the single-GPU minimum regardless.
- R285's cache Monitor-card gap was addressed by later 440e0851/subsequent server imports; the current Z/K server has conversation_cache_view. Its Windows Job Object finding remains a conditional OS-support difference.
- R285 host receipts (544 pass / 11 skip) apply to its adoption snapshot @ 501dd9ef, not to the later Z/K source. Finding a feature in a later source tree does not transfer old test status to it.
- R433, R441 and R442 correctly distinguish ancestry/history preservation from actual source adoption. The 45-parent preservation merge 8927eb69 makes commits reachable; it does not establish which product tree was selected. R441's J-to-Z conclusions use actual source/fixture evidence and explicitly do not claim feature/sycl synchronized. No report reviewed here justifies equating ancestry alone with implementation adoption.

### Performance evidence and comparability

Existing reports generally mark cross-engine/source comparisons as non-equivalent rather than claiming a direct ranking. Preserve those limits:

- R278's Niko v0.1.43 results (19.070/6.295 tok/s for cache 128; 17.773/8.480 for cache 512) are one diagnostic sample per arm, built with icpx 2026.1 and using serial read_windows8. They are not clean speed-eligible, and output IDs/LP5 differ. Its comparison with Xe's batched 8192 route on the free DPC++ build is explicitly not a controlled ranking.
- R395 v2's historical Strata SYCL layer-major pair (453.2935 vs 645.848 tok/s medians) is a valid repeated same-binary comparison within that old recipe. The current HTTP bench.sh row (384.8 prefill, 7.8 decode median) is a different source/compiler/binary/client and workload: 32,049 vs 32,768 input tokens, 24 vs one output, int8 KV/context 262,144 with resident 32,768 vs all-KV-resident/context 65,538, MMQ and route differences. R395 explicitly says this supports a source-regression hypothesis, not a measured 646-to-385 loss.
- R342/R344 explain that pristine upstream --long uses fresh approximately-32K prompts, caps output at 24 tokens, and records actual prompt_tokens. It is a short fresh-context decode sample, not sustained decode or guaranteed exact 32,768 input. A same client and same nominal setting do not make different engine/backend builds equivalent; record actual prompt length, source/build/runtime, route, KV/cache, output count, and per-arm samples.
- Target docs require using the upstream unchanged client for cross-project timing. Target's root bench.sh is a wrapper for that checkout's own tools/strata_bench.py; R442 correctly flags the need to state which checkout supplies the script. No reviewed R278/R395 report falsely treats the cited unlike rows as a controlled winner; the overreach is in the generic skill's acceptance rule, not those report conclusions.

### XeStrata-derived requirements that exceed this user's goal

- Z AGENTS.md encodes Xe's Intel Arc/B70/UHD 770 and AVX2 hardware matrix (lines 5-14), Debian free/contrib-llvm/contrib-icpx build/license matrix (16-41), all-mode test rules, package rules, and Xe branch retirement process. This Z CMake is also XeStrata/Linux-only and still identifies the 0.1.40.2 Xe base. Those rules describe that Xe product; they are not requirements for a personal Niko-based fork. Preserve upstream licensing and attribution obligations, but do not impose Xe's Debian three-mode architecture unless explicitly chosen.
- The generic .claude/skills/upstream-sync/SKILL.md is explicitly a Xe workflow: port CUDA/HIP changes (lines 3, 44, 49), build three modes (3, 97+), and require at most 1% loss on Intel, NVIDIA, and AMD GPUs (3, 11, 74, 198-205). This conflicts with no CUDA/HIP work, no Xe release contribution, and one personal PC as the performance target.
- The project strata-upstream-sync skill's separate rule that all non-inference features must be imported (current skill lines 30-34) also needs a user-scope gate. Its own integration guide correctly says to separate mandatory API fixes from optional inference changes, but “all” imports can still turn every upstream OS, multi-GPU, packaging, and platform-only feature into a false obligation. Keep a functional inventory; mark each item applicable to the chosen personal-PC OS/device/use, and port only applicable features or intentional fixes. XeStrata remains a benchmark/idea source, never a parity acceptance target.

## Recommended working contract

Use Niko1221/Strata as the sole release/source baseline and pin the selected Niko tag plus exact commit. Treat v0.1.43 @ 7695859 as a known reviewed pin until a newer official pin is deliberately selected. Build the personal fork's functional inventory from that upstream snapshot; keep CUDA/HIP outside implementation and validation scope. Use XeStrata source only to identify an optional architecture or measured benchmark idea, then validate it against the Niko-based fork and the user's actual PC. Keep server/CLI/settings behavior, kernel behavior, and benchmark results as distinct evidence. For each imported behavior, show the actual source/call path and its own test receipt; preserve stale report findings as historical snapshot results. For speed claims, use same hardware/model/input identity, client revision, route/config, output budget, and clean repeated samples; otherwise label the result a diagnostic or hypothesis and do not rank it.

## Sources read

R433, R434, R441, R442; R278, R285, R300, R302, R342, R344, R395 v2; relevant committed AGENTS.md, CMakeLists.txt, server/setup/skill source at the branch pins above. The supplied latest registry JSON was not opened. No raw logs/benchmark JSON were read.
role: read-only proposal; Main decisions are in decisions.json
